t hough as you fay very well promotion comes not from the eaft nor from the weft but it is god that
orders it in fuch way as he pleafes yet fince god does give nothing to us in vayne hee would not
have us to negled the making any of thofe oportunities which hee is pleafed to offerr us for our
good and therefore as wee are not to refift his will foe wee ought not to refift his difpenfations
which his divine providence houldes out to us i have now the opportunity offerred me of doing my
friend and thofe hee governes a publick good and of receving my felfe as i hope a privat advantage
by it either of which i doe fupofe i may juftifiably endeavour the one as the other the law of
nature teaching us felfeprefervation as well as the doing of others good wherefore i am not at all
afhamed to infift ftill in this letter upon what i did in mylaft which is that before i enter any
further into any matters i fhould bee glad to receive from your frind fome affurance at leaft of his
kindneffe and favour that i may not bee abfolutely throwne off to the wide world without friends or
fupport and that i may expeft to bee provided for by him after that i fhall have loft my felfe every
where elfe for his fake for though i cannot {beeaculo[n-]yreach[4a]ftrustsince} it is come to my
knowledge by {meerechance} and {(w?)ithouttheleastiniunctionof} fecrecy
{thepersonigoti(q?)o(w?)tfrom} taking it {forgranted} upon his meeting {meeasheethoug(x?)t} ftealing
out of whitehall {<england?>} that i was not only perticularly informed of {thematerbutalso}
employed in it yet fince it is the abfolute breaking of {apothhathaibeeneahtching} by
{the(w?)holepartieof_} there is noe queftion {butishal} by this one aflion render my felfe
{irreconciiablk(w?)iththemaslongaailite} and therfore certaynly when your friend fhall ferioufly
confider the nature of this matter hee cannot thinke it ftrange in me to expeft to bee aftured of
his proteftion before i fhall doe a thinge that will render it impoftible for mee to receive it any
where elfe i am very farr from having the leaft imagination in this of engaging your friend to a
promife of doing mee good upon the pretence of a fervice which afterwards i fhould not bee able to
doe i defire nothing from him till i have fhewne him by the {[efFe<5ls,]} that the fervice {(i?)}
intend to doe him is not inconfiderable and then hee will bee able to judge whether the fervice i
doe him bee worthy his thankes or noe sir i am in fuch haft to make an end for feare of loofing this
pofte that i feare you will fcarce be able to reade the hand much lefte that which is written in
cipher fince i doe not verry well know my felfe whether it bee true written or hoe and if this
correfpondence continue betweene us i fhould defire you to fende me another cipher this which you
have fent mee already being very imperfedt though it is more then tyme i fhould make an end i cannot
hinder myfelfe from reprefenting this to your confideration firft what defigne i can have in this
that i doe if it be not to linke myfelfe intirely to your friends intereft and fortune the part i
have a mind to aft if hee would give mee leave being fuch that it would bee impoftible for mee to
have dependance afterwards upon any body but himfelfe thouoh i fhould intend it never foe much next
whether or noe i have not reafbn to beleeve that your friend muft needs think how fmall a proportion
of parts foever god hath given mee i may bee ufefull to him in this perticular bufineffe confidering
the {(q?)ualitie} i am of the famihar acquaintance {(i?)} have amongft all the {<thecavaliers?>} and
the ihare i have hitherto had of theire bufinefte and laft whither or noe i ought in reafon to
expeft hee will admitt of mee if in this foe prelting a conjundure and wherein icaa without vanity
pretend to bee in fome kinde ufefull to him hee dos abfolutely rejedl the fervice i offer him j for
how flight foever you may make of thes bufineffe i know it is a more {<generalrising>} troope and in
which more {peopleareengagedtheninanioneof} the {formerones(w?)hatsoeutr} army {tha} by {the} it
{eis} in {ca} it {seat} and at the {eco} the {siderablei} the {<england?><which>the} am
{<have>notla} am {de<designs>tosurp} it {i} in {e} that by {he} am {hauegiuen(i?)alds} by {off} and
{rt} am thoufand armes {<which>l} am {readitobeemaceuse} and {f(w?)hentheirebusines} in
{eshalberipeforit} and which makes mee beleeve the time appointed for it is not farre off i have
been affured this day that {orm} and {nd} is in {<england?>h} am {dehashas} at {ritinto_} this plott
is foe infalible that noe difcovery can prevent it which would rather make mee beleeve it were a
rediculous one then any thing elfe if i did not know perticularly it were indeed foe well layd that
nothing but his and ignorance together could defiroye it i know very well too it would not bee hard
for mee to have as considerable a fhare in it as any body if the offers i have already mae of my
fervice to {<thelordprotector>} and the naturall averfion i have to fubmitt to thofe that have ufed
mee unworthily did not hinder mee from it sir it depends on your friend to difpofe of mee as hee
pleafes if he thinkes that what i have to fay may bee of ufe to him without doubt the beft way were
to let me come and wayte upon him it being certayne that i fhould bee better able to informe him of
this bufineife in one fingle difcourfe than i fhould be able to doe by a hundred feverall letters
befides i know very well that my fifter and fome others i would imploy would bee very inftrumentall
to mee in it who it would bee impoffible for mee to engage without being there myfelfe if your
friend thinkes it fitteft for mee to be there unknowne i am fure i could order my journey thither
foe that noe body in the world fliould fufped it being eafy for mee by the lieutenant gouvernors
meanes to goe out of this towne without being feene and afterwards as eafy to land fomewhere in
ingland where noe body knowes mee from thence to goe ftraight to london where your friend fhould
apointe mee were noe hard matter neither fliould i finde any more difficulty in keeping my chamber
there then to keepe it heere which i have done without llirring out once fince my coming to this
towne i fuppofe you will eafily perceive by the earneftneffe i write to you with about this matter
that my inclination leades me rather to come to you then to ftay heere i confeffe it does foe
becaufe i know i fhould bee able to doe your friend more fervice there then i can doe being in this
place and i am fure i fhould doe it with a greate deale of affeftion if your friend bee of the fame
opinion i fhall immediatly upon the leaft intimation of his that hee is willing to it come away in
what manner he fhall apoint mee but if for fom hidden caufes which i cannot guefle hee will not
confent to it i fhall then expedt from him at leaft that he will be pleafed to lett mee have under
hisowne hand fome aflurance of his favoure that i may hope the fervice i fhall doe him fhall not
abfolutely bee forgot but that in cafe i can contribute fomthing to his advantage hee will be
pleafed to owne mee as one who hee is willing he fhould hereafter depend upon his fortyne for it has
beene my lucke to bee very ill ufed by thofe i have deferved well from and therefore i am the more
excufable if i am a little too apprehenfive of meeting with the fame kind of ufage though in another
place and if out of that aprehenfion i am defirous before i {[en-]} gage myfelfe any fiirther in
this matter to have fome furety as to my owne perticular though the furety i now demaunde would bee
as i conceive but very fmale if i did not very much rely upon your friends generofity pray fir weigh
fearioufly what i have heere faid to you and lett mee have fpeedily your anfwer for i have nothinge
to doe heere but in order to this bufineffe in the meane tyme i afke your pardon for all this
trouble and defire you to bee affured that whatever fortune i runne or whether your friend fhall
thinke fit to accept of the fervice i offer him or noe i fhall however thinke myfelfe obliged by the
civilities you in your owne perticular have fhewed mee to bee as long as i live sir your moft
affeftionate and mofl humble fervant
